newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota forecasts $1.4 bln budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota forecasts $1.4 bln budget surplus.

text.p: A $1.4 billion budget surplus is in Minnesota's future, according to figures released this week by the state's finance department.
Gov. Arne Carlson is planning to propose a $500 million tax cut as a result of the projected surplus.

The state's finance department reported that a "robust economy" helped fuel a $522 million balance projected for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30. In addition, the department forecast a $468 million surplus in fiscal 1998 and another $448 million surplus in fiscal 1999.
"With a significant budget surplus, Minnesota's taxpayers deserve to have some of their money returned," Carlson said in a news relelase.
He said the $500 million in tax relief would be accomplished through a one-time income tax rebate, funded with one-third of the fiscal 1996-97 surplus and $240 million in budget cuts.
Carlson said the remainder of the projected $1.4 billion surplus would go to school aid reserve and to increase the state's budget reserve, which currently totals $261 million.
He cautioned that the the reserve was important in the event of an economic downturn.
In addition, he called for several goals in managing the state's budget including restoring the state's triple-A bond rating from all three rating agencies.

Minnesota is already rated triple-A by Fitch Investors Service and Moody's Investors Service, which upgraded the state's general obligation bond rating from Aa1 in May. Standard & Poor's Corp., however, rates the state AA-plus. Minnesota has about $2.1 billion of GO debt outstanding.
